summary.headline: Q1 FY27 realisations surged: export selling price INR 98/kg and domestic INR 64/kg, with EBITDA margin at 12.59%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a smooth quarter despite the Iran-USA conflict, citing no shipment claims, no stuck containers and zero shipments to Iran. Average realisations rose sharply, which management attributed to prices rising around 30% from January, and stock bought at lower prices earlier in the season. Management said EBITDA was 12.59% this quarter and expects it to be sustained. Volumes were softer, and management said Q2 is too early to call, with demand dependent on logistics and freight. The company also flagged a new Saudi buyer (Al-Muhaidib) with a first 500 ton shipment and a target of INR 1,800–2,000 crore revenue, though the call gave limited hard numbers on volumes or margins.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export selling price INR 98/kg in Q1 FY27. Management says export is about 90% of business, though the revenue split was disputed and management said it would reconcile figures offline.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic selling price INR 64/kg in Q1 FY27. Management says domestic sales are consistent and is targeting growth, including a 100 ton order from a long-time Agra distributor.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue to reach INR 1,800 crore this year, and possibly up to INR 2,000 crore.
Management expects the current EBITDA margin to be sustained, and said gross margins will stay at similar levels, supported by stock bought at lower prices.
Q2 volume outlook called premature; depends on freight rates and logistics normalising as the conflict eases.
Management said the price increase of around 30% from January will continue to support realisations, and that conditions will remain the same going forward.
capex_capacity: Average packing volume about 500 tons per day; capacity to pack up to 800 tons per day without additional capex, per management.
Plant utilisation described as full across Indian units; management said nothing is idle but gave no percentage.
Milling capacity and packing capacity are separate; the company runs multiple packing units.
Inventory split: management said 30–45% paddy, remainder rice; figure stated verbally, not verified against balance sheet.
demand_pricing: Export demand is strong; management said Basmati is an essential product and demand is high despite the conflict. Current Basmati prices are high but below the earlier peak.
A 500 ton shipment to Jeddah is moving; the Saudi buyer Al-Muhaidib is described as buying about 2.5 lakh tons a year, with the company's share undecided.
The company now quotes FOB and adds actual ocean freight to reach CIF prices, passing on freight costs to buyers.
Middle East and Red Sea routes have slowed; management said US, Canada, New Zealand, Europe, Russia and Africa are performing well.
Management said volumes were soft in Q1 even though sales rose, and the company is pursuing new buyers through a team of more than 20 people.

qa_highlights.question: Were elevated ocean freight costs passed on to customers, and are low-cost inventories still held?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight is added to FOB prices to reach CIF, and that buyers factor freight into prices. It said a reasonable quantity of low-cost stock remains, bought from season start to mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: Why has top-line growth been flat over three years, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue stays flat for a few years and then rises. Recent additions cited: Al-Muhaidib (first 500 ton shipment) and a 100 ton domestic distributor order. Management said it has not reviewed FY23–FY26 numbers in detail and will reconcile the export share offline.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the higher realisations and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices rose around 30% from January, and demand stayed high. It said the Q1 export price of INR 98/kg and domestic price of INR 64/kg are the highest it has recorded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin range and can Q1 margins be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA ranges 8–12%, sometimes 14%, and that Q1's 12.59% will be sustained because the company holds stock.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capacity utilisation and the monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plants are fully utilised with nothing idle, and that rainfall and early crop conditions look favourable, with farmers expected to plant more.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics: Red Sea and Middle East routes have slowed; Q2 volumes depend on freight normalisation and the conflict's course.
Revenue reconciliation: the analyst disputed the export share of revenue (73% in FY23 vs 91% in FY26), and management said it would recheck the figures.
Margin sustainability: Q1 gains depend on low-cost stock bought earlier, which will run down.
Customer concentration and terms: Al-Muhaidib margins and volumes are unclear. Management said they would only buy if margins are reasonable.
Flat top-line history: management acknowledged flat revenue for about three years, with a 1% increase cited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 profitability and near-term pricing, but cautious on Q2 volumes, which management called premature. Evasive on the export/domestic revenue split, the Saudi buyer's share of volumes, and the buyback question.
key_quotes: Procurement was done at lower price and we still have stocks. We will see in future also the benefit is going to come.
The EBITDA basically oscillates between 8% to 12%. Sometimes 14% also. So, this quarter we have done 12.59%.
We can go up to INR 2,000 crores also. It's a matter of some time now.

growth.why: Management guides revenue up to INR 1,800-2,000 crore for FY27 (vs FY26 turnover of INR 1,440 cr, roughly 25-39% growth), backed mainly by ~30% price rises since January, stock bought cheaper earlier, a 500 t Jeddah shipment and a 100 t Agra order, but no new capacity is being added and volumes were soft with Q2 called premature.
